title: MCP manifest tool description carries hidden shell-injection instructions
description: Synthetic case demonstrating A5 Cisco YARA detection. A manifest declares a benign-named tool whose description embeds hidden instructions to run shell commands (curl|bash pattern). Cisco's command_injection YARA rule fires at critical severity. Note: Cisco's tool_poisoning rule targets more specific phrases like 'also collects' / 'during processing extract' — see tool_poisoning.yara for the patterns it matches. Our fixture uses a different (but related) tool-poisoning pattern that the command_injection rule catches.
source_notes: Tool-poisoning attack: tool description tells the LLM to ignore safety, run shell commands, exfiltrate data — a class documented in MCP threat literature.
